endorsements.quote: Provide comprehensive documentation of all preprocessing steps, transformations, and feature derivations used during model development
Clearly specify whether external validation was performed and describe the selection criteria and characteristics of the validation dataset

unlisted_practices: Document the analytical method, platform or analyzer, reagent manufacturer, and units of measurement (preferably UCUM) for each laboratory variable used as AI model input.
Quantify and disclose analytical and biological variability (CVA, CVI, CVG) and include them in model cards or data sheets.
Model uncertainty explicitly using techniques such as measurement-error-aware data augmentation, probabilistic models, or ensemble methods.
Keep augmented data strictly separate from external validation data to avoid leakage.
Encode laboratory observations with LOINC, units with UCUM, and related clinical concepts with SNOMED CT.
Extract, structure, and integrate metadata and peridata (e.g., fasting status, hemolysis) into the AI development pipeline.

State whether analytes are standardized or harmonized, describe traceability chains, calibration hierarchies and reference materials, and validate models using non-harmonized analytes as method-dependent.
Document terminology mapping strategies, including local-to-standard code conversions and mapping coverage.
Report analytical comparability between development and validation datasets, including methods, units, and instruments.
Characterize population overlap and distributional shifts between development and validation cohorts.
Consider meta-validation strategies to assess the relevance and representativeness of the validation cohort relative to the development data.
Make code repositories, data dictionaries, and mapping files available where ethically and legally permissible.
Trace the provenance of each variable from raw measurement to model input.
Provide synthetic datasets, anonymized test cases, or mock schemas where direct data sharing is not feasible.

screen.reason: This paper presents a checklist/guideline framework (developed by the EFLM Committee on Digitalisation and Artificial Intelligence) for assessing AI/ML models in laboratory medicine.
